evidence.title: A review of lithium ion battery failure mechanisms and fire prevention strategies
evidence.abstract: Abstract Lithium ion batteries (LIBs) are booming due to their high energy density, low maintenance, low self-discharge, quick charging and longevity advantages. However, the thermal stability of LIBs is relatively poor and their failure may cause fire and, under certain circumstances, explosion. The fire risk hinders the large scale application of LIBs in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. This manuscript provides a comprehensive review of the thermal runaway phenomenon and related fire dynamics in singe LIB cells as well as in multi-cell battery packs. Potential fire prevention measures are also discussed. Mitigating the hazards associated with a growing number of LIB applications represents a significant new challenge for the fire safety engineering community. Some perspectives and outlooks on the future of LIB fire safety research and safety engineering are given.

evidence.title: Electric Vehicle Battery Pack Design for Mitigating Thermal Runaway Propagation
evidence.abstract: The production of electric vehicle battery packs with ever-increasing energy densities has accelerated the electrification of the world’s automotive industry. With increased attention on the electric vehicle markets, it is vital to increase the safety of these vehicles which now hold higher hazardous potential. This paper aims to explore the field of pack-level thermal runaway mechanisms and evaluate potential mitigation strategies. Most available literature concentrates on the micromanagement of thermal runaway whereas this paper takes a more holistic approach. Thermal simulations for analysing thermal runaway of modules in differing locations are run to characterise the behaviour of a thermal runaway event at pack-level. Results suggest that the propagation of thermal runaway is consistently severe in a cooling plate cooled battery pack as the cooling plate acts as a channel for high temperatures. Additionally, thermal insulation added to contain the rapid increase in temperature unfortunately results in wider spread higher temperatures

The process was conducted in a microwave radiation field having a high energy density of 5 W/mL and over a time less than 2 minutes. The sample measurements included: powder X-ray diffraction, density, specific surface area, and chemical composition. The morphology and structure were investigated by scanning electron microscopy as well as transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The thermal behavior analysis was conducted using a simultaneous thermal analysis technique coupled with quadruple mass spectrometry. Additionally, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy tests of heated samples were performed. A degradation test and a biocompatibility study in vitro using human osteoblast cells were also conducted. The developed method enables the synthesis of pure, fully crystalline hexagonal HAp nanopowder with a specific surface area close to 240 m2/g and a Ca/P molar ratio equal to 1.57. TEM measurements showed that this method results in particles with an average grain size below 6 nm. A 28-day degradation test conducted according to the ISO standard indicated a 22% loss of initial weight and a calcium ion concentration at 200 &micro;mol/dm3 in the tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane hydrochloride test solution. A quantitative analysis was based on the 2,3-bis-(2-methoxy-4-nitro-5-sulfophenyl)-2H-tetrazolium-5-carboxanilide. Viability assay as well as on DNA content measurements in the PicoGreen test. evidence.title: Rainfall induced erosion of soils used in earth roads
evidence.abstract: Earth roads in rural areas of the developing world are key engines to the development of countries. They give access to education and health services, sustain agriculture and businesses, and promote social interactions between communities. However, earth roads suffer substantially from poor engineering and funding for construction and maintenance. Rainfall is probably their most dangerous enemy resulting in soil particle detachment leading to the loss of surface material. A laboratory rainfall simulator was used to identify the performance of an earth road surface compacted at the maximum dry density against rainfall energy and surface flow. Under the rain intensity of 30mm/hr, erosion increased with rain duration from 0 to 30 minutes. Fine sand (0.06 – 0.02mm) and medium sand (0.02 – 0.6mm) particles eroded faster than coarse sand (0.6 – 2mm) and gravel (> 2mm) particles of the sediments collected at 5 minutes intervals of time. Additionally, a 20cm x 20cm photograph at the same place was analysed using ImageJ software and showed reduction in number of particles from 18554 at 10 min to 5803 at 25 min as smaller particles had eroded in the meantime.

evidence.title: Developement of an apparatus for practical calibration of heat flux sensors
evidence.abstract: Heat flux sensors are focused related to energy conservation. They are convenient tools which can detect direction and amount of heat flux. It is necessary to determine sensitivity of heat flux sensors before they are used. The sensitivity is a relation coefficient between heat flow density and output voltage of sensor. The steady state method is used to determine it in many cases. National Metrology Institute of Japan (NMIJ) of National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) is supplying calibration service for heat flux sensors using by a Guarded Hot Plate (GHP) apparatus. The measurement with GHP apparatus takes long time more than one week although it gives reliable result with small uncertainty. In order to solve this problem, the small apparatus for practical calibration of heat flux sensors was developed according to the steady state method. The apparatus has beautiful steady temperature gradient in the volume of 30 mm × 30 mm x 30 mm. The cover made by expanded polypropylene is effective to decrease heat loss. It takes about 40 minutes to be steady state. Uncertainty of sensitive coefficient estimation using this apparatus was roughly evaluated less than 10% with the coverage factor k = 2.

evidence.title: Safety Studies for Approval of Green Ammonia Bunkering Terminals – How Best to Apply CFD Modelling
evidence.abstract: Green ammonia (NH3) produced by hydrogen from water electrolysis using renewable electricity is considered to have an important role in the ambitions to decarbonize the maritime sector. With a boiling point of -33.4 °C, much closer to ambient temperatures than LH2, NH3 is less complicated to handle and to store. While the low flammability of NH3 represents a challenge as a fuel, this is an advantage regarding handling, and the volumetric energy density of NH3 is almost 50% higher than for LH2. A disadvantage with NH3 is its toxicity and odour, already at 5-50 ppm most people will recognize its characteristic odour, and at concentrations of 1% in air NH3 may be fatal within minutes. For a successful introduction of NH3 as a maritime fuel, safe handling is critical. To shorten the construction time and increase flexibility related to scale-up to meet possible future increasing demands, AZANE Fuel Solutions has developed a bunkering concept with NH3 stored in floating barges permanently moored at the bunkering site. With partial support from the Research Council of Norway the bunkering concept has been further developed, one of the key tasks was to ensure a best possible safety level of the terminal. To achieve this the NH3 is stored refrigerated near its boiling point with all penetrations on top and redundant cooling systems. The tank is further well protected against impact with B/5 separation from the hull of the barge. For the siting studies the NH3 toxicity is the primary concern, and as the terminal will store more NH3 than 200 tonnes, the Seveso-III upper tier major accident legislation applies. To develop required risk contours for the approval, all possible loss of containment scenarios must be evaluated considering expected leak rates and durations from statistical rupture and hole size frequency distributions. These scenarios must be evaluated considering the actual geometry and terrain and actual distribution of wind speed and direction. The toxic dose fatality probability contribution must then be assessed using probit functions considering exposure concentration and duration for each leak scenario, wind direction, wind speed and distance. evidence.title: Bioinspired Zonal Nanogrids for the Internet of Things: A Dimensionless Design Framework from Milliwatt Wearables to Watt-Scale Clusters
evidence.abstract: The Internet of Things is projected to reach 39 billion devices by 2030, creating a battery bottleneck that demands a shift toward energy autonomy. Photovoltaic conversion is the only harvesting modality common to every scale, appearing on the human body, on vehicles, and at buildings, whereas thermoelectric, piezoelectric, biofuel, and regenerative sources are each confined to particular scales. We propose a zonal nanogrid architecture for wearables, robotics, electric vehicles, and buildings, grounded in hierarchical microgrid control as well as bioinspired embodied and distributed energy concepts, and reduce it to three dimensionless design numbers, namely the zonal transport number ΠT, the autonomy number α and the embodiment number β. ΠT is evaluated over 6.5 decades, from a 3.33 mW wearable node to a 10 kW whole-building nanogrid that bounds the domain of architectural advantage, while all three numbers span 4.8 decades. Together they yield a sizing criterion, Areq = Eload/(ηstorage·H), where ηstorage is the storage efficiency and H the daily harvested energy per unit area, defining the minimum harvester area for supply adequacy. In worked examples, 1 m² of window-integrated indoor photovoltaics brings a room-level sensor cluster to the supply-adequacy frontier (α = 0.99), whereas the full addressable load (~4.91 W) would require 72 m², unachievable indoors. Distributed harvesting reduces relative distribution losses by 31.3% in wearables and 40% in the vehicular auxiliary domain, where structural storage reaches β = 0.62. The framework sets quantitative efficiency and area targets for indoor, flexible and structurally integrated photovoltaics, and identifies the scales at which the architecture provides advantages.

evidence.title: HDR-DTCP: High-Dynamic-Range Differential Tissue-Coupled Wireless Powering for Tunable Biphasic Stimulation in Injectable Implants
evidence.abstract: Next-generation implantable neurostimulators require efficient wireless power delivery in smaller, less invasive form factors, yet variations in tissue coupling, implantation conditions, and stimulation loads can alter received power (or requirements) and degrade energy-harvesting performance. This work presents high-dynamic-range (HDR) differential tissue-coupled powering (DTCP), termed HDR-DTCP, a body-coupled architecture in which noninvasive differential electrodes establish an AC electric field in tissue and a thread-like implant extracts power from the longitudinal potential gradient for on-chip harvesting and stimulation. Distributed coupling along the implant length, rather than receiver cross-section, enables minimally invasive injectable geometries, with harvested power scaling with implant length. A 65-nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) prototype integrates a reconfigurable four-stage energy harvester with automatic stage selection and a tunable constant-current biphasic stimulator, achieving 63.5\% peak power-conversion efficiency (PCE) at $-16.3$ dBm and $>50\%$ PCE over a 9-dB input-power range. Preliminary in-vivo validation of DTCP was done with a second application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) on an injectable flexible substrate, capable of being delivered through a 14-gauge needle adjacent to the sciatic nerve of Sprague-Dawley rats (n=4). External copper-pad DTCP powering evoked repeatable hind-limb twitches and electromyography (EMG) response; ultrasound confirmed sub-millimeter nerve proximity, video-based paw-tip tracking captured the response, and 8-day post-implant dissection verified placement along the sciatic-nerve trajectory. Overall, this work provides an integrated wireless powering, energy-harvesting, and stimulation platform toward fully battery-free injectable neuromodulation implants.

evidence.title: Development of an Advanced 3-Layer Nerve-Connecting Bio-Smart Contact Lens for Surgical-Free Vision Restoration and DNA-Locked Biometric Privacy
evidence.abstract:
आविष्कारक का नाम: बंटी कुमावत

आविष्कार का नाम: एडवांस्ड नर्व-कनेक्टिंग बायो-स्मार्ट लेंस (Advanced Nerve-Connecting Bio-Smart Lens)

 

वैज्ञानिक लेख (Technical Article & Blueprint)

 

 

1. परिचय (Introduction)

 

यह आविष्कार दृष्टिहीनता (Blindness) के उपचार में एक युगांतरकारी कदम है। यह तकनीक बिना किसी जटिल न्यूरो-सर्जरी, ब्रेन चिप (जैसे कि न्यूरालिंक) या भारी चश्मे के, सीधे आंखों की नसों को सक्रिय करके प्राकृतिक दृष्टि वापस लाने की क्षमता रखती है। यह लेंस तीन परतों (3-Layer Matrix) पर काम करता है जो सुरक्षा, प्राइवेसी और सटीक दृष्टि का एक अनूठा संगम है।

 

2. लेंस के निर्माण की सामग्री (Materials Required)

 

इस लेंस को बनाने के लिए अत्याधुनिक नैनोटेक्नोलॉजी और जैव-सामग्रियों (Biomaterials) का उपयोग किया जाएगा:

• ग्राफीन (Graphene): आउटर लेयर के लिए, जो अत्यधिक पतली, पारदर्शी और बेहतरीन विद्युत चालक (Electrical Conductor) है।

• क्वांटम डॉट्स / नैनो-क्रिस्टल्स (Nano-Crystals): प्रकाश की तरंगों (Wavelengths) को पकड़ने और फ़िल्टर करने के लिए।

• सिंथेटिक पेप्टाइड्स (Synthetic Peptides): कृत्रिम प्रोटीन श्रृंखला जो डीएनए बाइंडिंग में मदद करती है।

• मरीज के स्वयं के स्टेम सेल्स (Patient's Autologous Stem Cells): कॉर्निया के साथ जैविक तालमेल बिठाने के लिए।

• बायो-कंपैटिबल कंडक्टिव पॉलीब्यूटिलीन (Bio-compatible Conductive Polybutylene): नसों तक सिग्नल पहुंचाने के लिए एक सुरक्षित, लचीला और सुचालक पॉलीमर।

• कृत्रिम न्यूरो-ट्रांसमीटर (Artificial Neurotransmitters): एसिटाइलकोलाइन (Acetylcholine) या ग्लूटामेट जैसे बायो-केमिकल्स जो नसों को उत्तेजित करते हैं।

 

3. लेंस की आंतरिक संरचना और परतों का निर्माण (How It Is Made)

 

लेंस को तीन अति-सूक्ष्म परतों को आपस में जोड़कर (Layer-by-Layer Nanofabrication) बनाया जाएगा:

• बाहरी परत (Outer Layer - बायो-हार्वेस्टर): इसमें ग्राफीन के बेस पर नैनो-क्रिस्टल्स को व्यवस्थित किया जाता है। यह परत आंख के आंसुओं में मौजूद ग्लूकोज और बाहरी प्रकाश से ऊर्जा लेकर खुद को चार्ज रखती है (Self-Powering)।

• मध्यम परत (Middle Layer - DNA मैचिंग मैट्रिक्स): सिंथेटिक पेप्टाइड्स के ऊतकों को मरीज के लैब-ग्रोन स्टेम सेल्स के साथ एकीकृत किया जाता है। इसमें एक विशिष्ट बायो-कोडिंग स्लॉट होता है जहाँ मरीज का डीएनए डेटा स्टोर होता है।

• आंतरिक परत (Inner Layer - न्यूरो-ट्रांसमीटर इंटरफेस): पॉलीब्यूटिलीन की एक बेहद महीन परत जो कृत्रिम न्यूरो-ट्रांसमीटर के नैनो-रिलीज़र्स (Micro-dispensers) से जुड़ी होती है। यह परत सीधे आंख की ऑप्टिक नर्व (नस) के संपर्क में रहती है।

evidence.title: Analysis of Lithium-ion Battery Cells Degradation Based on Different Manufacturers
evidence.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are recognised as a key technology to power electric vehicles and integrate grid-connected renewable energy resources. The economic viability of these applications is affected by the battery degradation during its lifetime. This study presents an extensive experimental degradation data for lithium-ion battery cells from three different manufactures (Sony, BYD and Samsung). The Sony and BYD cells are of LFP chemistry while the Samsung cell is of NMC. The capacity fade and resistance increase of the battery cells are quantified due to calendar and cycle aging. The charge level and the temperature are considered as the main parameters to affect calendar aging while the depth of discharge, current rate and temperature for cycle aging. It is found that the Sony and BYD cells with LFP chemistry has calendar capacity loss of nearly 5% and 8% after 30 months respectively. Moreover, the Samsung NMC cell reached 80% state of health after 3000 cycles at 35C and 75% discharge depth suggesting a better cycle life compared to the other two battery cells with the same conditions

evidence.title: Detailed Thermal Characterization on a 48V Lithium-Ion Battery Pack during Charge-Discharge Cycles
evidence.abstract: This study experimentally investigates the temperature distribution and behavior of a 48V Lithium-Ion (Li-ion) battery pack during two charge-discharge cycles using 25 thermocouples. Results indicate that better convective heat transfer occurs at the external surfaces of the pack, while middle cells reach maximum temperatures. Differences are also observed in the behavior of the three modules. The discharge cycle shows a temperature rise of 5.8°C with a pack temperature gradient increasing from 1.3°C to 2.7°C. The study highlights the importance of assessing the thermal behavior of each module and the complexity of the Li-ion battery pack system. Findings on the battery cells, modules, and pack in the same study can provide valuable insights for designing efficient cooling systems for Li-ion battery packs.

evidence.title: Anisotropic thermal characterisation of large-format lithium-ion pouch cells
evidence.abstract: Temperature strongly impacts battery performance, safety and durability, but modelling heat transfer requires accurately measured thermal properties. Herein we propose new approaches to characterise the heat capacity and anisotropic thermal-conductivity components for lithium-ion pouch cells. Heat capacity was estimated by applying Newton's law of cooling to an insulated container within which the cell was submerged in warmed dielectric fluid. Thermal conductivity was quantified by heating one side of the cell and measuring the opposing temperature distribution with infra-red thermography, then inverse modelling with the anisotropic heat equation. Experiments were performed on commercial 20 Ah lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pouch cells. At 100% state-of-charge (SOC), the heat capacity of a 489 g, 224 mL pouch cell was 541 J/K. The through-plane and in-plane thermal conductivities were respectively 0.52 and 26.6 W/(mK). Capturing anisotropies in conductivity is important for accurate thermal simulations. State-of-charge dependence was also probed by testing at 50% SOC: the heat capacity dropped by 6% and thermal conductivity did not significantly change.

evidence.title: Numerical modeling of thermal runaway in high-energy lithium-ion battery packs induced by multipoint heating
evidence.abstract: Thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries is a primary safety concern in electric vehicles (EVs). Herein, a numerical thermal abuse model is proposed that integrates ordinary differential equations (ODEs), heat-transfer partial differential equations (PDEs), natural convection in computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and thermal radiation to investigate thermal propagation in a battery pack. A three-dimensional geometric model of a high-energy lithium-ion battery pack comprising 18,650 format cells was constructed to analyze the thermal characteristics using the finite element method (FEM). A thermal abuse test was conducted to simulate the spread of thermal runaway in cells owing to multipoint heating. The maximum differences in the peak temperature between the proposed model and the model without convection were -150 K and 52.0 s, respectively, while the differences between the proposed model and the model without radiation were -52.4 K and -125.0 s, respectively. Furthermore, four additional models with different cell-to-cell gaps were constructed to study the thermal propagation characteristics, showing that the presence of a cell-to-cell gap accelerated heat transfer but compromised energy density for the battery pack. Ultimately, the coupling model at the pack level proposed in this study can improve the design of battery thermal management systems

evidence.title: An Acausal Li-Ion Battery Pack Model for  Automotive Applications
evidence.abstract: In this work, a novel acausal and reconfigurable battery pack model is presented. The model structure adopted for the battery cell is based on an equivalent circuit representation. The circuit elements are modified to take account of both hysteresis and diffusion limitation. The latter is known to be a nonlinear function of large operating currents or long operating times. It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

evidence.title: Testing and characterisation of large high-energy lithium-ion batteries for electric and hybrid electric vehicles
evidence.abstract: This thesis considers the drivetrain and battery system requirements of Hybrid Electric Vehicles. The data herein proves that a series hybrid electric drivetrain with Lithium-ion batteries and plug-in recharge promises to be viable and sustainable. However, for mass production of series HEVs comprehensive performance characteristics and prediction of ageing behaviour of Lithium-ion batteries is essential but currently not available.The main part of the thesis, following a graphical comparison of different energy storage solutions, is a detailed treatise on large Li-ion batteries. Construction and Li-ion working principles are summarised, together with several effects such as Peukert and memory effects, ageing of Li-ion cells, their temperature dependence and safety, and limits of charging/discharging.Preliminary performance tests on 50 and 100 Ah Li-ion cells showed the necessity for a careful investigation of suitable reference conditions in order to achieve reproducibly precise results from repeated discharge/charge cycles. Then the main tests result in detailed graphs and tables of the discharge and charge characteristics. These main tests include effects of rate of discharge, energy-efficiency, temperature, resting time between test-cycles, hysteresis, ageing, and degradation. A new testing method that is based on the step response technique is suggested and investigated to whether it gives a meaningful but rapid measure of open circuit voltage and equivalent circuit models of the battery. Statistically significant theoretical models, equations and graphs are included.The Appendix gives summaries of the author's seven main publications and presentations dealing with Systems Approach and five publications on Large Li-ion batteries, followed by most of these in full

system.value: Electric Vehicle Battery Pack Design for Mitigating Thermal Runaway Propagation

abstract.value: The production of electric vehicle battery packs with ever-increasing energy densities has accelerated the electrification of the world’s automotive industry. With increased attention on the electric vehicle markets, it is vital to increase the safety of these vehicles which now hold higher hazardous potential. This paper aims to explore the field of pack-level thermal runaway mechanisms and evaluate potential mitigation strategies. Most available literature concentrates on the micromanagement of thermal runaway whereas this paper takes a more holistic approach. Thermal simulations for analysing thermal runaway of modules in differing locations are run to characterise the behaviour of a thermal runaway event at pack-level. Results suggest that the propagation of thermal runaway is consistently severe in a cooling plate cooled battery pack as the cooling plate acts as a channel for high temperatures. Additionally, thermal insulation added to contain the rapid increase in temperature unfortunately results in wider spread higher temperatures

system.value: Highly biocompatible, nanocrystalline hydroxyapatite synthesized in a solvothermal process driven by high energy density microwave radiation

abstract.value: Dariusz Smolen1, Tadeusz Chudoba1, Iwona Malka1, Aleksandra Kedzierska1, Witold Lojkowski1, Wojciech Swieszkowski2, Krzysztof Jan Kurzydlowski2, Malgorzata Kolodziejczyk-Mierzynska3, Malgorzata Lewandowska-Szumiel31Polish Academy of Science, Institute of High Pressure Physics, Warsaw, Poland; 2Faculty of Materials Engineering, Warsaw University of Technology, Warsaw, Poland; 3Department of Histology and Embryology, Center of Biostructure Research, Medical University of Warsaw, Warsaw, PolandAbstract: A microwave, solvothermal synthesis of highly biocompatible hydroxyapatite (HAp) nanopowder was developed. The process was conducted in a microwave radiation field having a high energy density of 5 W/mL and over a time less than 2 minutes. The sample measurements included: powder X-ray diffraction, density, specific surface area, and chemical composition. The morphology and structure were investigated by scanning electron microscopy as well as transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The thermal behavior analysis was conducted using a simultaneous thermal analysis technique coupled with quadruple mass spectrometry. Additionally, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy tests of heated samples were performed. A degradation test and a biocompatibility study in vitro using human osteoblast cells were also conducted. The developed method enables the synthesis of pure, fully crystalline hexagonal HAp nanopowder with a specific surface area close to 240 m2/g and a Ca/P molar ratio equal to 1.57. TEM measurements showed that this method results in particles with an average grain size below 6 nm. A 28-day degradation test conducted according to the ISO standard indicated a 22% loss of initial weight and a calcium ion concentration at 200 &micro;mol/dm3 in the tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane hydrochloride test solution. The cytocompatibility of the obtained material was confirmed in a culture of human bone derived cells, both in an indirect test using the material extract, and in direct contact. A quantitative analysis was based on the 2,3-bis-(2-methoxy-4-nitro-5-sulfophenyl)-2H-tetrazolium-5-carboxanilide. Viability assay as well as on DNA content measurements in the PicoGreen test. Indirect observations were performed at one point in time according to the ISO standard for in vitro cytotoxicity (ie, after 24 hours of cell exposure to the extracts). The direct contact

system.value: Analysis of Lithium-ion Battery Cells Degradation Based on Different Manufacturers

abstract.value: Lithium-ion batteries are recognised as a key technology to power electric vehicles and integrate grid-connected renewable energy resources. The economic viability of these applications is affected by the battery degradation during its lifetime. This study presents an extensive experimental degradation data for lithium-ion battery cells from three different manufactures (Sony, BYD and Samsung). The Sony and BYD cells are of LFP chemistry while the Samsung cell is of NMC. The capacity fade and resistance increase of the battery cells are quantified due to calendar and cycle aging. The charge level and the temperature are considered as the main parameters to affect calendar aging while the depth of discharge, current rate and temperature for cycle aging. It is found that the Sony and BYD cells with LFP chemistry has calendar capacity loss of nearly 5% and 8% after 30 months respectively. Moreover, the Samsung NMC cell reached 80% state of health after 3000 cycles at 35C and 75% discharge depth suggesting a better cycle life compared to the other two battery cells with the same conditions

system.value: Detailed Thermal Characterization on a 48V Lithium-Ion Battery Pack during Charge-Discharge Cycles

abstract.value: This study experimentally investigates the temperature distribution and behavior of a 48V Lithium-Ion (Li-ion) battery pack during two charge-discharge cycles using 25 thermocouples. Results indicate that better convective heat transfer occurs at the external surfaces of the pack, while middle cells reach maximum temperatures. Differences are also observed in the behavior of the three modules. The discharge cycle shows a temperature rise of 5.8°C with a pack temperature gradient increasing from 1.3°C to 2.7°C. The study highlights the importance of assessing the thermal behavior of each module and the complexity of the Li-ion battery pack system. Findings on the battery cells, modules, and pack in the same study can provide valuable insights for designing efficient cooling systems for Li-ion battery packs.

system.value: Numerical modeling of thermal runaway in high-energy lithium-ion battery packs induced by multipoint heating

abstract.value: Thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries is a primary safety concern in electric vehicles (EVs). Herein, a numerical thermal abuse model is proposed that integrates ordinary differential equations (ODEs), heat-transfer partial differential equations (PDEs), natural convection in computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and thermal radiation to investigate thermal propagation in a battery pack. A three-dimensional geometric model of a high-energy lithium-ion battery pack comprising 18,650 format cells was constructed to analyze the thermal characteristics using the finite element method (FEM). A thermal abuse test was conducted to simulate the spread of thermal runaway in cells owing to multipoint heating. The maximum differences in the peak temperature between the proposed model and the model without convection were -150 K and 52.0 s, respectively, while the differences between the proposed model and the model without radiation were -52.4 K and -125.0 s, respectively. Furthermore, four additional models with different cell-to-cell gaps were constructed to study the thermal propagation characteristics, showing that the presence of a cell-to-cell gap accelerated heat transfer but compromised energy density for the battery pack. Ultimately, the coupling model at the pack level proposed in this study can improve the design of battery thermal management systems

system.value: An Acausal Li-Ion Battery Pack Model for  Automotive Applications

abstract.value: In this work, a novel acausal and reconfigurable battery pack model is presented. The model structure adopted for the battery cell is based on an equivalent circuit representation. The circuit elements are modified to take account of both hysteresis and diffusion limitation. The latter is known to be a nonlinear function of large operating currents or long operating times. It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

system.value: Testing and characterisation of large high-energy lithium-ion batteries for electric and hybrid electric vehicles

abstract.value: This thesis considers the drivetrain and battery system requirements of Hybrid Electric Vehicles. The data herein proves that a series hybrid electric drivetrain with Lithium-ion batteries and plug-in recharge promises to be viable and sustainable. However, for mass production of series HEVs comprehensive performance characteristics and prediction of ageing behaviour of Lithium-ion batteries is essential but currently not available.The main part of the thesis, following a graphical comparison of different energy storage solutions, is a detailed treatise on large Li-ion batteries. Construction and Li-ion working principles are summarised, together with several effects such as Peukert and memory effects, ageing of Li-ion cells, their temperature dependence and safety, and limits of charging/discharging.Preliminary performance tests on 50 and 100 Ah Li-ion cells showed the necessity for a careful investigation of suitable reference conditions in order to achieve reproducibly precise results from repeated discharge/charge cycles. Then the main tests result in detailed graphs and tables of the discharge and charge characteristics. These main tests include effects of rate of discharge, energy-efficiency, temperature, resting time between test-cycles, hysteresis, ageing, and degradation. A new testing method that is based on the step response technique is suggested and investigated to whether it gives a meaningful but rapid measure of open circuit voltage and equivalent circuit models of the battery. Statistically significant theoretical models, equations and graphs are included.The Appendix gives summaries of the author's seven main publications and presentations dealing with Systems Approach and five publications on Large Li-ion batteries, followed by most of these in full

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
cemetery_warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Thermal runaway propagation via conductive heat transfer through cell-to-cell contact points** (domain knowledge: pouch cells in packs exhibit localized hotspots at contact interfaces; record evidence: thermal runaway dynamics in multi-cell packs)
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: **Insert thermally insulating, electrically conductive composite interlayers (e.g., SiC-coated aluminum oxide) between pouch cells** (domain knowledge: thermal barriers reduce heat flux; record evidence: fire dynamics in multi-cell packs require mitigation)

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Exothermic reaction amplification via electrolyte vapor pressure buildup in sealed pouch cells** (domain knowledge: separator collapse increases local pressure; record evidence: thermal runaway linked to fire dynamics in single cells)
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: **Add passive pressure-relief vents (0.1–0.3 mm orifice) with flame-retardant seals (e.g., intumescent polymer) to each pouch cell** (domain knowledge: venting reduces internal pressure; record evidence: fire prevention requires mitigating thermal instability)

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Electrothermal feedback loop acceleration via lithium plating at high C-rates** (domain knowledge: NMC cathodes + graphite anodes prone to plating at >2C; record evidence: thermal runaway linked to poor thermal stability)
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: **Implement adaptive charge current modulation (AI-driven) to dynamically reduce C-rate during thermal precursor detection (ΔT ≥ 5°C/min)** (domain knowledge: plating mitigation via current limiting; record evidence: fire prevention requires addressing thermal instability)

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Thermal decoupling via modular segmentation** — Domain knowledge: thermal runaway propagation is driven by conductive/convection heat transfer between cells; record evidence: cooling plates exacerbate propagation by acting as heat channels. Mechanism: segment the pack into thermally isolated modules (e.g., via air gaps or compliant thermal barriers) to interrupt lateral heat transfer while preserving internal module cooling.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Replace the monolithic cooling plate with **modular cooling blocks separated by 2–3 mm air gaps**, each block servicing a 4-cell submodule. Add low-conductivity (k < 0.2 W/m·K) silicone-based thermal barriers between modules to block conduction while allowing local cooling.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Active thermal siphoning** — Domain knowledge: natural convection in air is insufficient to dissipate high heat fluxes; record evidence: insulation worsens propagation by trapping heat. Mechanism: leverage **forced air siphoning** between modules to actively draw heat away from failing cells without relying on conductive paths.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Introduce **perpendicular airflow channels** between cell layers, connected to a low-pressure manifold that siphons hot air upward via a stack-effect chimney. Use **porous metal foam inserts** (porosity 95%, k = 0.5 W/m·K) between cells to enhance turbulent mixing without blocking cooling airflow.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Phase-change thermal shunt** — Domain knowledge: latent heat absorption can temporarily absorb excess heat; record evidence: conductive paths (cooling plates) accelerate propagation. Mechanism: embed **phase-change material (PCM) shunts** between cells to absorb heat during separator collapse, delaying temperature rise in neighbors.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Insert **PCM sheets (n-eicosane, melting point 36°C, ΔH = 240 J/g)** between every 2nd cell layer, with **micro-perforations** to allow gas venting while retaining PCM. Pair with **localized cooling jets** targeting PCM regions to reset temperature post-event.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: The same **rapid, high-energy-density volumetric heating mechanism** (microwave-driven solvothermal synthesis) is mapped to a **localized, high-frequency electromagnetic field** (e.g., inductive or capacitive coupling) to induce **selective thermal stabilization of the separator** near the cathode-electrolyte interface, suppressing exothermic decomposition pathways by maintaining a **nanoscale thermal gradient** that prevents bulk separator collapse. Domain knowledge: thermal runaway in NMC cells is initiated by separator melting (onset ~130°C), driven by localized Joule heating; the source system’s **5 W/mL energy density in <2 min** implies a **spatially confined, high-power-density input** that avoids bulk overheating.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Embed **nanocrystalline ceramic particles (e.g., Al₂O₃ or SiO₂, grain size <10 nm)** into the separator matrix, where they act as **microwave-absorbing nuclei** under an applied **pulsed high-frequency electromagnetic field (100 kHz–1 MHz, 1–5 W/cm³)** during fast charge. The field is **gated to activate only at >2.5V per cell** (threshold for thermal instability).

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: The **solvothermal nucleation mechanism** (formation of **fully crystalline, defect-free nanoparticles in <2 min**) is mapped to **in-situ synthesis of a thermally stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer** via **microwave-assisted electrolyte decomposition**, replacing the conventional SEI with a **nanocrystalline ceramic barrier** that inhibits lithium dendrite penetration and separator degradation. Domain knowledge: SEI instability is a primary failure mode in fast-charged NMC cells; the source system’s **hexagonal HAp crystallinity** suggests a **low-defect, high-thermal-stability** phase.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Replace the baseline carbonate-based electrolyte with a **sol-gel precursor mixture (e.g., lithium bis(oxalato)borate + microwave-absorbing nanoparticles)** that, under **pulsed microwave irradiation (2.45 GHz, 1 W/mL for 60 s)**, forms a **~50 nm thick Li₃PO₄-based SEI** on the anode surface. The process is triggered at **>3.5V per cell** (onset of SEI formation).

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: The **controlled degradation mechanism** (22% mass loss over 28 days with **stable calcium ion release**) is mapped to a **sacrificial thermal buffer layer** in the separator, where **nanocrystalline particles** absorb heat via **endothermic phase transitions** (e.g., dehydration or crystallization) before separator melting occurs. Domain knowledge: thermal runaway in NMC cells is propagated by **exothermic reactions (e.g., SEI decomposition at ~100°C, cathode exotherms at ~200°C)**; the source system’s **200 µmol/dm³ Ca²⁺ release** implies a **self-limiting degradation pathway**.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Coat the separator with a **5 µm layer of lithium-aluminum-silicate (LAS) nanoparticles (grain size <10 nm, loading 10 wt%)**, where the particles undergo **endothermic dehydration at ~150°C** (absorbing ~1.2 kJ/g) before the baseline separator (PP/PE) melts (~130°C). The coating is applied via **spray-drying with a microwave-curable binder**.

hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Insert **aluminum nitride (AlN) or boron nitride (BN) composite sheets** between pouch cells in the stack, with thickness 0.2–0.5 mm and thermal conductivity >150 W/m·K, positioned to intercept heat flux from a failing cell before it reaches adjacent separators.

CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.justification: R377 patent-text ground truth (TOSCANINI/R377_PATENT_TEXT_FETCH.json + R377_PATENT_TEXT_GROUND_TRUTH.json): 12/30 family representatives (40%) were substantively irrelevant cross-domain term collisions (CWDM optical link for a battery-thermal candidate; dental-condition monitoring for rolling stock; bone fracture forceps for rail steel...). A hit sharing NO entity term with the candidate now needs >= 3 NON-generic mechanism terms to be mechanism art: the measured true cross-domain analog (line-pipe steel with hydrogen fracture toughness for a rail-steel candidate) shares 3 non-generic terms and survives; every measured false positive shares <= 2 and is demoted. This RAISES the cross-domain bar (was the same >= 2 as same-domain) — stricter, not weaker (Art. VII).
CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap remains a proxy; entity word-sense collisions ('gear': steering vs draft) can still pass — disclosed limitation, not a solved problem

MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.justification: same term-overlap rule family as the pipeline relevance adjudicator and the Q2 instrument (>= 2 shared content terms = domain-specific rather than accidental collision); NOT weakened relative to any prior gate
MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap is a proxy for mechanism identity

ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.justification: a family ANTICIPATES only when nearly ALL elements of the candidate's FULL distinguishing set (uncapped — the claim elements, not the 6-term query core) appear in the family's claim/abstract text; 0.8 leaves a >= 20% element margin — anything lower would convert partial art into a kill (Art. XXVIII forbids). Measured adversarial case: a domain-only patent reached 0.857 against a capped denominator whose true differentiators (acoustic, multi-modal) had been ranked out
ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.uncertainty: claim coverage measured by term overlap, not a claim chart; recorded per family with evidence tier

MAX_QUERY_TERMS.justification: provider-measured sweet spot for keyword patent queries (longer queries dilute ranking)

ABSTRACT_TIER_MIN_CHARS.justification: below ~80 chars a snippet carries title echoes, not mechanism description; it cannot support an abstract-tier coverage decision

search_execution.note: status is derived from execution, not findings: a failed/timeout query set can never support a no-match claim (R394 s2/s4, Art. XXI.3)

CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.justification: R377 patent-text ground truth (TOSCANINI/R377_PATENT_TEXT_FETCH.json + R377_PATENT_TEXT_GROUND_TRUTH.json): 12/30 family representatives (40%) were substantively irrelevant cross-domain term collisions (CWDM optical link for a battery-thermal candidate; dental-condition monitoring for rolling stock; bone fracture forceps for rail steel...). A hit sharing NO entity term with the candidate now needs >= 3 NON-generic mechanism terms to be mechanism art: the measured true cross-domain analog (line-pipe steel with hydrogen fracture toughness for a rail-steel candidate) shares 3 non-generic terms and survives; every measured false positive shares <= 2 and is demoted. This RAISES the cross-domain bar (was the same >= 2 as same-domain) — stricter, not weaker (Art. VII).
CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap remains a proxy; entity word-sense collisions ('gear': steering vs draft) can still pass — disclosed limitation, not a solved problem

MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.justification: same term-overlap rule family as the pipeline relevance adjudicator and the Q2 instrument (>= 2 shared content terms = domain-specific rather than accidental collision); NOT weakened relative to any prior gate
MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap is a proxy for mechanism identity

ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.justification: a family ANTICIPATES only when nearly ALL elements of the candidate's FULL distinguishing set (uncapped — the claim elements, not the 6-term query core) appear in the family's claim/abstract text; 0.8 leaves a >= 20% element margin — anything lower would convert partial art into a kill (Art. XXVIII forbids). Measured adversarial case: a domain-only patent reached 0.857 against a capped denominator whose true differentiators (acoustic, multi-modal) had been ranked out
ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.uncertainty: claim coverage measured by term overlap, not a claim chart; recorded per family with evidence tier

MAX_QUERY_TERMS.justification: provider-measured sweet spot for keyword patent queries (longer queries dilute ranking)

ABSTRACT_TIER_MIN_CHARS.justification: below ~80 chars a snippet carries title echoes, not mechanism description; it cannot support an abstract-tier coverage decision

determinism.rule: identical problem + identical relevant evidence set + identical relevance model must yield the identical verdict; any divergence is classified NON_DETERMINISTIC and disclosed, never silently resolved (R396 P6 / R394 s3)

custody_records.raw_content: Abstract Lithium ion batteries (LIBs) are booming due to their high energy density, low maintenance, low self-discharge, quick charging and longevity advantages. However, the thermal stability of LIBs is relatively poor and their failure may cause fire and, under certain circumstances, explosion. The fire risk hinders the large scale application of LIBs in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. This manuscript provides a comprehensive review of the thermal runaway phenomenon and related fire dynamics in singe LIB cells as well as in multi-cell battery packs. Potential fire prevention measures are also discussed. Mitigating the hazards associated with a growing number of LIB applications represents a significant new challenge for the fire safety engineering community. Some perspectives and outlooks on the future of LIB fire safety research and safety engineering are given.

custody_records.raw_content: Earth roads in rural areas of the developing world are key engines to the development of countries. They give access to education and health services, sustain agriculture and businesses, and promote social interactions between communities. However, earth roads suffer substantially from poor engineering and funding for construction and maintenance. Rainfall is probably their most dangerous enemy resulting in soil particle detachment leading to the loss of surface material. A laboratory rainfall simulator was used to identify the performance of an earth road surface compacted at the maximum dry density against rainfall energy and surface flow. Under the rain intensity of 30mm/hr, erosion increased with rain duration from 0 to 30 minutes. Fine sand (0.06 – 0.02mm) and medium sand (0.02 – 0.6mm) particles eroded faster than coarse sand (0.6 – 2mm) and gravel (> 2mm) particles of the sediments collected at 5 minutes intervals of time. Additionally, a 20cm x 20cm photograph at the same place was analysed using ImageJ software and showed reduction in number of particles from 18554 at 10 min to 5803 at 25 min as smaller particles had eroded in the meantime.

custody_records.raw_content: Heat flux sensors are focused related to energy conservation. They are convenient tools which can detect direction and amount of heat flux. It is necessary to determine sensitivity of heat flux sensors before they are used. The sensitivity is a relation coefficient between heat flow density and output voltage of sensor. The steady state method is used to determine it in many cases. National Metrology Institute of Japan (NMIJ) of National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) is supplying calibration service for heat flux sensors using by a Guarded Hot Plate (GHP) apparatus. The measurement with GHP apparatus takes long time more than one week although it gives reliable result with small uncertainty. In order to solve this problem, the small apparatus for practical calibration of heat flux sensors was developed according to the steady state method. The apparatus has beautiful steady temperature gradient in the volume of 30 mm × 30 mm x 30 mm. The cover made by expanded polypropylene is effective to decrease heat loss. It takes about 40 minutes to be steady state. Uncertainty of sensitive coefficient estimation using this apparatus was roughly evaluated less than 10% with the coverage factor k = 2.

A disadvantage with NH3 is its toxicity and odour, already at 5-50 ppm most people will recognize its characteristic odour, and at concentrations of 1% in air NH3 may be fatal within minutes. For a successful introduction of NH3 as a maritime fuel, safe handling is critical. With partial support from the Research Council of Norway the bunkering concept has been further developed, one of the key tasks was to ensure a best possible safety level of the terminal. To achieve this the NH3 is stored refrigerated near its boiling point with all penetrations on top and redundant cooling systems. The tank is further well protected against impact with B/5 separation from the hull of the barge. For the siting studies the NH3 toxicity is the primary concern, and as the terminal will store more NH3 than 200 tonnes, the Seveso-III upper tier major accident legislation applies. These scenarios must be evaluated considering the actual geometry and terrain and actual distribution of wind speed and direction. The toxic dose fatality probability contribution must then be assessed using probit functions considering exposure concentration and duration for each leak scenario, wind direction, wind speed and distance. custody_records.raw_content: The Internet of Things is projected to reach 39 billion devices by 2030, creating a battery bottleneck that demands a shift toward energy autonomy. Photovoltaic conversion is the only harvesting modality common to every scale, appearing on the human body, on vehicles, and at buildings, whereas thermoelectric, piezoelectric, biofuel, and regenerative sources are each confined to particular scales. We propose a zonal nanogrid architecture for wearables, robotics, electric vehicles, and buildings, grounded in hierarchical microgrid control as well as bioinspired embodied and distributed energy concepts, and reduce it to three dimensionless design numbers, namely the zonal transport number ΠT, the autonomy number α and the embodiment number β. ΠT is evaluated over 6.5 decades, from a 3.33 mW wearable node to a 10 kW whole-building nanogrid that bounds the domain of architectural advantage, while all three numbers span 4.8 decades. Together they yield a sizing criterion, Areq = Eload/(ηstorage·H), where ηstorage is the storage efficiency and H the daily harvested energy per unit area, defining the minimum harvester area for supply adequacy. In worked examples, 1 m² of window-integrated indoor photovoltaics brings a room-level sensor cluster to the supply-adequacy frontier (α = 0.99), whereas the full addressable load (~4.91 W) would require 72 m², unachievable indoors. Distributed harvesting reduces relative distribution losses by 31.3% in wearables and 40% in the vehicular auxiliary domain, where structural storage reaches β = 0.62. The framework sets quantitative efficiency and area targets for indoor, flexible and structurally integrated photovoltaics, and identifies the scales at which the architecture provides advantages.

custody_records.raw_content: Next-generation implantable neurostimulators require efficient wireless power delivery in smaller, less invasive form factors, yet variations in tissue coupling, implantation conditions, and stimulation loads can alter received power (or requirements) and degrade energy-harvesting performance. This work presents high-dynamic-range (HDR) differential tissue-coupled powering (DTCP), termed HDR-DTCP, a body-coupled architecture in which noninvasive differential electrodes establish an AC electric field in tissue and a thread-like implant extracts power from the longitudinal potential gradient for on-chip harvesting and stimulation. Distributed coupling along the implant length, rather than receiver cross-section, enables minimally invasive injectable geometries, with harvested power scaling with implant length. A 65-nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) prototype integrates a reconfigurable four-stage energy harvester with automatic stage selection and a tunable constant-current biphasic stimulator, achieving 63.5\% peak power-conversion efficiency (PCE) at $-16.3$ dBm and $>50\%$ PCE over a 9-dB input-power range. Preliminary in-vivo validation of DTCP was done with a second application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) on an injectable flexible substrate, capable of being delivered through a 14-gauge needle adjacent to the sciatic nerve of Sprague-Dawley rats (n=4). External copper-pad DTCP powering evoked repeatable hind-limb twitches and electromyography (EMG) response; ultrasound confirmed sub-millimeter nerve proximity, video-based paw-tip tracking captured the response, and 8-day post-implant dissection verified placement along the sciatic-nerve trajectory. Overall, this work provides an integrated wireless powering, energy-harvesting, and stimulation platform toward fully battery-free injectable neuromodulation implants.

आविष्कारक का नाम: बंटी कुमावत

आविष्कार का नाम: एडवांस्ड नर्व-कनेक्टिंग बायो-स्मार्ट लेंस (Advanced Nerve-Connecting Bio-Smart Lens)

 

वैज्ञानिक लेख (Technical Article & Blueprint)

 

 

1. परिचय (Introduction)

 

यह आविष्कार दृष्टिहीनता (Blindness) के उपचार में एक युगांतरकारी कदम है। यह तकनीक बिना किसी जटिल न्यूरो-सर्जरी, ब्रेन चिप (जैसे कि न्यूरालिंक) या भारी चश्मे के, सीधे आंखों की नसों को सक्रिय करके प्राकृतिक दृष्टि वापस लाने की क्षमता रखती है। यह लेंस तीन परतों (3-Layer Matrix) पर काम करता है जो सुरक्षा, प्राइवेसी और सटीक दृष्टि का एक अनूठा संगम है।

 

2. लेंस के निर्माण की सामग्री (Materials Required)

 

इस लेंस को बनाने के लिए अत्याधुनिक नैनोटेक्नोलॉजी और जैव-सामग्रियों (Biomaterials) का उपयोग किया जाएगा:

• ग्राफीन (Graphene): आउटर लेयर के लिए, जो अत्यधिक पतली, पारदर्शी और बेहतरीन विद्युत चालक (Electrical Conductor) है।

• क्वांटम डॉट्स / नैनो-क्रिस्टल्स (Nano-Crystals): प्रकाश की तरंगों (Wavelengths) को पकड़ने और फ़िल्टर करने के लिए।

• सिंथेटिक पेप्टाइड्स (Synthetic Peptides): कृत्रिम प्रोटीन श्रृंखला जो डीएनए बाइंडिंग में मदद करती है।

• मरीज के स्वयं के स्टेम सेल्स (Patient's Autologous Stem Cells): कॉर्निया के साथ जैविक तालमेल बिठाने के लिए।

• बायो-कंपैटिबल कंडक्टिव पॉलीब्यूटिलीन (Bio-compatible Conductive Polybutylene): नसों तक सिग्नल पहुंचाने के लिए एक सुरक्षित, लचीला और सुचालक पॉलीमर।

• कृत्रिम न्यूरो-ट्रांसमीटर (Artificial Neurotransmitters): एसिटाइलकोलाइन (Acetylcholine) या ग्लूटामेट जैसे बायो-केमिकल्स जो नसों को उत्तेजित करते हैं।

 

3. लेंस की आंतरिक संरचना और परतों का निर्माण (How It Is Made)

 

लेंस को तीन अति-सूक्ष्म परतों को आपस में जोड़कर (Layer-by-Layer Nanofabrication) बनाया जाएगा:

• बाहरी परत (Outer Layer - बायो-हार्वेस्टर): इसमें ग्राफीन के बेस पर नैनो-क्रिस्टल्स को व्यवस्थित किया जाता है। यह परत आंख के आंसुओं में मौजूद ग्लूकोज और बाहरी प्रकाश से ऊर्जा लेकर खुद को चार्ज रखती है (Self-Powering)।

• मध्यम परत (Middle Layer - DNA मैचिंग मैट्रिक्स): सिंथेटिक पेप्टाइड्स के ऊतकों को मरीज के लैब-ग्रोन स्टेम सेल्स के साथ एकीकृत किया जाता है। इसमें एक विशिष्ट बायो-कोडिंग स्लॉट होता है जहाँ मरीज का डीएनए डेटा स्टोर होता है।

• आंतरिक परत (Inner Layer - न्यूरो-ट्रांसमीटर इंटरफेस): पॉलीब्यूटिलीन की एक बेहद महीन परत जो कृत्रिम न्यूरो-ट्रांसमीटर के नैनो-रिलीज़र्स (Micro-dispensers) से जुड़ी होती है। यह परत सीधे आंख की ऑप्टिक नर्व (नस) के संपर्क में रहती है।

custody_records.raw_content: Lithium-ion batteries are recognised as a key technology to power electric vehicles and integrate grid-connected renewable energy resources. The economic viability of these applications is affected by the battery degradation during its lifetime. This study presents an extensive experimental degradation data for lithium-ion battery cells from three different manufactures (Sony, BYD and Samsung). The Sony and BYD cells are of LFP chemistry while the Samsung cell is of NMC. The capacity fade and resistance increase of the battery cells are quantified due to calendar and cycle aging. The charge level and the temperature are considered as the main parameters to affect calendar aging while the depth of discharge, current rate and temperature for cycle aging. It is found that the Sony and BYD cells with LFP chemistry has calendar capacity loss of nearly 5% and 8% after 30 months respectively. Moreover, the Samsung NMC cell reached 80% state of health after 3000 cycles at 35C and 75% discharge depth suggesting a better cycle life compared to the other two battery cells with the same conditions

custody_records.raw_content: This study experimentally investigates the temperature distribution and behavior of a 48V Lithium-Ion (Li-ion) battery pack during two charge-discharge cycles using 25 thermocouples. Results indicate that better convective heat transfer occurs at the external surfaces of the pack, while middle cells reach maximum temperatures. Differences are also observed in the behavior of the three modules. The discharge cycle shows a temperature rise of 5.8°C with a pack temperature gradient increasing from 1.3°C to 2.7°C. The study highlights the importance of assessing the thermal behavior of each module and the complexity of the Li-ion battery pack system. Findings on the battery cells, modules, and pack in the same study can provide valuable insights for designing efficient cooling systems for Li-ion battery packs.

custody_records.raw_content: Temperature strongly impacts battery performance, safety and durability, but modelling heat transfer requires accurately measured thermal properties. Herein we propose new approaches to characterise the heat capacity and anisotropic thermal-conductivity components for lithium-ion pouch cells. Heat capacity was estimated by applying Newton's law of cooling to an insulated container within which the cell was submerged in warmed dielectric fluid. Thermal conductivity was quantified by heating one side of the cell and measuring the opposing temperature distribution with infra-red thermography, then inverse modelling with the anisotropic heat equation. Experiments were performed on commercial 20 Ah lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pouch cells. At 100% state-of-charge (SOC), the heat capacity of a 489 g, 224 mL pouch cell was 541 J/K. The through-plane and in-plane thermal conductivities were respectively 0.52 and 26.6 W/(mK). Capturing anisotropies in conductivity is important for accurate thermal simulations. State-of-charge dependence was also probed by testing at 50% SOC: the heat capacity dropped by 6% and thermal conductivity did not significantly change.

custody_records.raw_content: Thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries is a primary safety concern in electric vehicles (EVs). Herein, a numerical thermal abuse model is proposed that integrates ordinary differential equations (ODEs), heat-transfer partial differential equations (PDEs), natural convection in computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and thermal radiation to investigate thermal propagation in a battery pack. A three-dimensional geometric model of a high-energy lithium-ion battery pack comprising 18,650 format cells was constructed to analyze the thermal characteristics using the finite element method (FEM). A thermal abuse test was conducted to simulate the spread of thermal runaway in cells owing to multipoint heating. The maximum differences in the peak temperature between the proposed model and the model without convection were -150 K and 52.0 s, respectively, while the differences between the proposed model and the model without radiation were -52.4 K and -125.0 s, respectively. Furthermore, four additional models with different cell-to-cell gaps were constructed to study the thermal propagation characteristics, showing that the presence of a cell-to-cell gap accelerated heat transfer but compromised energy density for the battery pack. Ultimately, the coupling model at the pack level proposed in this study can improve the design of battery thermal management systems

custody_records.raw_content: In this work, a novel acausal and reconfigurable battery pack model is presented. The model structure adopted for the battery cell is based on an equivalent circuit representation. The circuit elements are modified to take account of both hysteresis and diffusion limitation. The latter is known to be a nonlinear function of large operating currents or long operating times. It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

custody_records.raw_content: This thesis considers the drivetrain and battery system requirements of Hybrid Electric Vehicles. The data herein proves that a series hybrid electric drivetrain with Lithium-ion batteries and plug-in recharge promises to be viable and sustainable. However, for mass production of series HEVs comprehensive performance characteristics and prediction of ageing behaviour of Lithium-ion batteries is essential but currently not available.The main part of the thesis, following a graphical comparison of different energy storage solutions, is a detailed treatise on large Li-ion batteries. Construction and Li-ion working principles are summarised, together with several effects such as Peukert and memory effects, ageing of Li-ion cells, their temperature dependence and safety, and limits of charging/discharging.Preliminary performance tests on 50 and 100 Ah Li-ion cells showed the necessity for a careful investigation of suitable reference conditions in order to achieve reproducibly precise results from repeated discharge/charge cycles. Then the main tests result in detailed graphs and tables of the discharge and charge characteristics. These main tests include effects of rate of discharge, energy-efficiency, temperature, resting time between test-cycles, hysteresis, ageing, and degradation. A new testing method that is based on the step response technique is suggested and investigated to whether it gives a meaningful but rapid measure of open circuit voltage and equivalent circuit models of the battery. Statistically significant theoretical models, equations and graphs are included.The Appendix gives summaries of the author's seven main publications and presentations dealing with Systems Approach and five publications on Large Li-ion batteries, followed by most of these in full
